clue.text: Substance that may be of importance

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the verb for being significant

explanation.surface: A material that might turn out to be significant.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a noun, the second a verb, joined by 'that may'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names physical stuff as a noun, and as a verb means to count or be significant.

clue.text: Cat went up round injured lion, having night vision

indicators.note: the cat goes round the other pieces, enclosing them
in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: something injured is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cat climbing around a wounded lion, able to see in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed cat opens between its second and third letters to hold the jumbled lion. 'having night vision' is a playful definition: a moonlit scene can be seen at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonlit scene is lit by the moon, so it can be seen at night.

clue.text: A memento from Stoke Newington

indicators.note: taking a part from the place names means the letters are inside those words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words of the place name

explanation.surface: A souvenir picked up in Stoke Newington, a district of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a keepsake or souvenir kept as a reminder.

clue.text: Rubs out swear words about one

indicators.note: about means around, so the swear words surround the other piece

parts.note: effs, from the euphemism eff, are swear words
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: Someone erases curses written about a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eff' is the sounded-out first letter of a well-known swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: To efface is to erase or wipe away.

clue.text: Well established equestrian centre

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a building where horses are kept

explanation.surface: A riding school with a long and solid history.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means firm and steady; as a noun it is a building for housing horses.

clue.text: For example, start moving the dartboards

indicators.note: when things are moving their order changes, so the letters rearrange

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for for example
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub instruction to begin moving the dartboards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dartboard is the target at which darts are thrown.

clue.text: Uncovered a feature of the canopy

parts.note: bald means bare or uncovered
taken as written
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Revealing a part of the canopy's design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' means part of the face, not a characteristic.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldachin is an ornamental canopy over an altar, throne or doorway.

clue.text: Spilt ale on it through high spirits

indicators.note: spilt liquid is splashed about out of shape, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Beer slopped over something because of a drinker's merry mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a feeling of great joy, the same as being in high spirits.

clue.text: The energy with which six go over the old town

parts.note: Roman numeral six
taken as written
Ur is the ancient city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Six people setting off energetically for the old town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places the first pieces above the last in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigour is physical strength and energy.

clue.text: Big turnaround in front of gunners' officer — roof rack wobbling outside British base

indicators.note: 'outside' means the jumbled rack goes around the rest
'wobbling' says the letters of roof rack shake into a new order
'in front of' puts the reversed word ahead of the gunners and officer
'turnaround' says the word big is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: the RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A big U-turn ahead of an army officer while a wobbly roof rack surrounds a base.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled roof rack splits into two parts that go either side of everything else. Gibraltar is a British overseas territory with a military base.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibraltar, crowned by its rock, is a British overseas territory long used as a naval and military base.

clue.text: One gets nothing back among the hundreds getting treatment here

indicators.note: among means placed amid, so the pieces sit between the hundreds

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two hundreds give two Cs

indicators.note: back signals the nothing word is turned round

parts.note: nil means nothing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone getting nothing in return among a crowd of hundreds.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a place where patients get medical attention, often as outpatients.

clue.text: Like a musical, the Ring is epic art and moving

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

indicators.note: things that are moving shift position, so the letters change their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wagner's Ring cycle praised as epic, stirring art, like a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Ring' tempts toward Wagner, which suits the definition; here the ring is just the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Operatic describes something in the style of opera, a dramatic work set to music, as a musical is.

clue.text: Spray area towards skinflint

parts.note: abbreviation for area
to means towards
a skinflint is a stingy person

explanation.surface: Someone directing a spray at a mean person.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser is a device that turns liquid into a fine spray, as for perfume.

clue.text: Mistreat chap who takes in new worker

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so the male word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a chap is a male
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A man hiring a new employee and treating them badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To manhandle is to treat someone roughly or push them about physically.

clue.text: Enigmatic riddler gets vote after Henry nips off

indicators.note: something gone off has turned bad, so the letters it follows are scrambled

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
taken as written
a cross marks a vote on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A mysterious puzzler casts a vote once Henry has popped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nips off' reads as Henry leaving; the vote comes after the scrambled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Sphinx posed a riddle to travellers and killed those who failed to answer it.

clue.text: Stretches one's neck to see the birds

definitions.meaning: first meaning: extends the head forward to get a better view
second meaning: tall wading birds with long necks

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher leans forward to get a look at some birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to strain the neck forward; the noun names long-legged wading birds.

clue.text: Declaim printed data

definitions.meaning: first meaning: speak written words aloud to others
second meaning: information displayed by a machine

explanation.walkthrough: The two-word phrasal verb and the one-word noun share letters; the hyphen in the count covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means to recite text out loud; as a noun it is a display of information from an instrument.

clue.text: Adds salt from the springs

definitions.meaning: second meaning: spring is one of the four times of year

explanation.surface: Someone salting water drawn from the springs.
explanation.definitionFit: To season food is to flavour it; spring is one of the year's four divisions.

clue.text: Someone needed to get motion considered

definitions.text: Someone needed to get motion considered

parts.words: Someone needed to get motion considered
parts.note: surface reading: movement, perhaps a bowel motion needing a doctor; setter's reading: a formal proposal at a meeting is debated only once a second person backs it

explanation.walkthrough: 'motion' suggests physical movement, but it is a proposal in a formal meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: In meeting procedure a proposal needs a supporter besides the proposer before it can be debated.

clue.text: Provide flattering background for start of race

definitions.meaning: first meaning: show something to advantage by contrast
second meaning: the moment of starting out on a journey or race

explanation.surface: A scenic backdrop that flatters runners at the start of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a jewel is to enhance it by contrast; a set-off is also an act of starting out.

clue.text: Tom takes in nude floor show

indicators.note: taking something in holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
bare means naked

explanation.surface: A man named Tom watches a nude floor show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name, but it is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret is entertainment performed in a restaurant or nightclub while the audience sits at tables.

clue.text: Attempts to foster involved original father

indicators.note: something involved is tangled and complicated, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the original part of a word is its beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: only the first letter of father is used

explanation.surface: Attempts to foster a child involved the original father.
explanation.definitionFit: Efforts are tries or attempts to achieve something.

clue.text: Do something after moving a cart causes a fall

indicators.note: moving shifts the letters around into another order

parts.note: taken as written
to act is to do something

explanation.surface: Taking action after moving a cart brings on a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the action at the end, following the jumbled cart letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataract is a large waterfall, where a river drops steeply.

clue.text: Lawyers' underwear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in slang, a brief is a lawyer, so this is the possessive plural

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about legal attire; the two words are separate meanings. 'Brief' is British slang for a barrister or solicitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawyers are informally called briefs after the case papers they take; the word also names short underpants.

clue.text: Draw conclusions of hell, no less

indicators.note: less means minus, so the word before it is taken away

parts.note: the inferno is hell
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: Someone working out what hell is like, no more and no less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no less' reads as an emphatic phrase but means remove the letters of 'no'.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to deduce or reach a conclusion from evidence.

clue.text: Icy welcome from fliers over motorway? That's novel

parts.note: icy means very cold
a welcome relief or consolation

indicators.note: turning over flips the word so it is read from the end

parts.note: the Royal Air Force, the fliers
M is the British motorway prefix, as in M1

explanation.surface: A frosty reception from pilots flying above a motorway, called a novel experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's novel' looks like a remark about something new; it defines a book. Stella Gibbons's 1932 comic novel is set on a gloomy Sussex farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold Comfort Farm is the title of a famous English comic novel by Stella Gibbons.

clue.text: Twice set out to fly

indicators.note: out means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder as written

indicators.note: twice says the same rearranging of set is done a second time, giving the same block again

explanation.surface: Someone setting out two times to take a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: SET rearranged gives TSE, and taken twice it makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African biting insect, a fly that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Is furious and causes decay over manuscript

indicators.note: turned over, the word is read the other way round

parts.note: rots means decays or causes decay
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: An author raging as their manuscript decays.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm is to rage or show violent anger.
